message.content: The largest planet that has been observed and confirmed in our universe is the protoplanet **HD 100546 b**. It orbits the young star HD 100546 and is still in the process of forming. Its radius is estimated to be about **2.5–3 times that of Jupiter**, making it roughly 10–12 × larger than the largest planet in our own Solar System (Jupiter). Because it is a protoplanet, its mass is still growing, but current measurements suggest it is already several times more massive than Jupiter as well.
